display.title: Washing Negel Vasser: Little Zalman's Homework
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains why we wash negel vasser each morning, then tells of little Zalman, who shows his mother exactly how to wash and say the brachah, with a song to remember it.
display.summary_long: A clip from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on the Shulchan Aruch. Uncle Yossi reviews the first steps of the Jewish morning: thinking of Hashem as soon as we wake up, saying Modeh Ani, and then washing the hands with a large cup, just as the Kohen washed his hands and feet before entering the Mishkan to serve Hashem. Then comes a short story. Zalman's mother finds him splashing at a basin of water and learns that this is his homework: his teacher brought a basin, a two-handled cup and a towel to class. Zalman shows her how to take the cup in the right hand, pass it to the left, and pour on each hand in turn, three times, and he recites the brachah al netilas yadayim with its meaning. A song about the mitzvah follows, and Uncle Yossi reminds everyone to do mitzvos with joy, especially as Purim approaches.
display.lesson: Begin every day by washing negel vasser properly, so you serve Hashem in purity, and do every mitzvah with joy.

date.note: Cut from episode 517, one week before episode 518 (3 March 1992, 'tomorrow night is Rosh Chodesh Adar Sheni'); 'getting closer to Purim'.
